claim: RAUC v1.15.2 built natively for arm64 from the pinned commit with Debian 13 libraries produced a rauc binary with sha256 7f076b8b8ab7882dd4522952d511354c9d23690280945965ec14ad0009639d1f, byte-identical to the arm64 build in LAB-rauc-1152 (same commit, same Debian package versions): the RAUC build is reproducible

k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 arm64 artifacts verify against the release's sha256sum-arm64.txt: k3s-arm64 a779ccf1e5e2e33a62f5a29c2f1c0bbf99431e100579d4c10f0aa0742a6aa84b, k3s-airgap-images-arm64.tar.zst ca384f1a77aa83024bd82ad26fa4774971adb038e656a3b5b9af926be445a442 (equal to the Pi 5 kit pins)

Debian 13 arm64 kernel linux-image-6.12.116+deb13-arm64 (6.12.116-1) is a 4K-page ARM64 Image and ships the i6300esb watchdog module; on QEMU's virt machine with -device i6300esb -action watchdog=reset, a frozen init that armed /dev/watchdog was reset 3 times in about 146 s

Lab (Debian 13 arm64 guest, QEMU 11.1.3 with HVF on Apple M5 Max, GRUB arm64-efi, 2 full runs on one build): with RAUC 1.15.2 (bundle-formats=verity), k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 arm64 and the unchanged fresh-signal gate, the T1-T11 suite of LAB-rauc-1152 passed: good update committed after 3 fresh passes; k3s-broken and stale-Ready updates rolled back at the 300 s deadline with no input; kernel panic and watchdog hang tried 3 times then fell back and were never retried; power cut mid-install (59-61% of RAUC progress, before activation) and in the commit window recovered without input; wrong-key and plain bundles refused with no trial marker

Under native arm64 virtualization (HVF) a good update committed 31 s after the trial gate started (first fresh pass at 10-11 s), versus 81 s and 87-148 s in the x86_64 TCG labs; each 490 MB verity bundle installed in 29-30 s with guest writes throttled to 60 MiB/s

Nested KVM inside a Lima vz VM on Apple M5 Max gave erratic guest speed for this workload: in run 2 the gate's 300 s check window took 411 s of wall time and k3s was not fresh-healthy in time on a clean first boot, while an earlier diagnostic boot of the same disk passed in 61 s; the gate deadline is wall-clock, so a slow host can turn a good trial into a rollback
The Raspberry Pi 5 / 500 / CM5 firmware defaults to loading kernel_2712.img, which has Pi 5-specific optimisations including a 16K page size; if absent, kernel8.img is loaded

Debian AAVMF 2025.02-8+deb13u1 (AAVMF_CODE.fd sha256 5d3147294c56...52d3) hung after its banner when used with host QEMU 11.1.3 -accel hvf on macOS 27.2; Homebrew QEMU's bundled EDK2 (edk2-stable202408) booted the same disk to the gate [cause not investigated; lab tooling only]

The 9 gate files (onemind-health-gate, onemind-k3s-check, rauc-pre-install, bad-hang-init, 3 units, API responder, manifests) ran byte-identical on x86_64 (LAB-rauc-1152) and arm64; the only guest-side change was the serial console name in the GRUB template

On arm64 the naive (API-status-only) gate committed a k3s with no kubelet after 3 passes in 30 s in both runs (curl localhost:10248/healthz failed on the committed slot), reproducing the stale-Ready trap seen on x86 with RAUC and Rugix

Inference, not tested: because Raspberry Pi tryboot is one-shot [C-LAB-rauc-1152-012], a power cut during the trial boot on a Pi 5 returns to the old slot and the gate's fell-back mode marks the update bad; the GRUB 3-try retry shown in T9 does not carry over to the Pi 5 path
